description: Passkeys (WebAuthn) for your website. Client and server in one npm package, zero runtime dependencies, every check the WebAuthn specification asks for.
rules: Import PasskeyServer from 'passkify/server' on the server and register/login from 'passkify/client' in the browser. Importing the package root in browser code no longer fails — since verification moved to WebCrypto it bundles fine — it just ships the whole server verifier, roughly six times the size of the client half.

`origin` needs the scheme and, when non-default, the port ('https://example.com', 'http://localhost:3000'). `rpID` is a bare hostname with no scheme, port or path, and must be the origin's host or a registrable parent of it.

Never pass a username from the request body when the user already has a session. `{ username }` creates a new account and throws credential_exists for an existing one; adding a second passkey to a signed-in account uses `{ userId }` taken from the session.

finishRegistration and finishAuthentication throw on failure — they never return { verified: false }. Branch on error.code, never on the message text, and re-throw anything that is not a PasskeyError.
MemoryStore is for development only. Across more than one worker it produces intermittent challenge_not_found, because the challenge is issued by one process and redeemed by another.
A successful verification is not a session. The application must issue its own session in the onLogin/onRegister hook, or the ceremony succeeds and nothing happens.
